subject: zoology
question_text: What are the adverse effects of tobacco?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.43, SAQ 43). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: How tobacco is used
lines: Tobacco is used in three ways. It is smoked, it
is chewed as gutkha, and it is taken as snuff.
Tobacco contains nicotine, which is an alkaloid.
steps.why: The harm changes with the way tobacco enters the body, so naming the three forms first sets up the different effects described in the rest of the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing only about smoking. Chewing and snuff are two more forms and carry marks.
Leaving out nicotine. It is the substance behind most of the effects.
steps.memory_tip: Three ways in: smoked, chewed, snuffed. One substance behind them: nicotine.
steps.margin_note: Two short lines. Name all three forms and the alkaloid.

steps.label: Effect on blood and heart
lines: Smoking increases the carbon monoxide level in
the blood and reduces the oxygen level, so less
Nicotine stimulates the adrenal gland to release
raise the blood pressure and the heart rate.
steps.why: Two different substances do two different things here — carbon monoxide changes what the blood carries, nicotine changes what the heart does — and the examiner expects both routes.
common_mistakes: Writing that nicotine reduces the oxygen. Carbon monoxide does that.
Naming the hormones without saying what they do. State the rise in blood pressure and heart rate.
steps.memory_tip: Carbon monoxide works on the blood, nicotine works through the adrenal gland on the heart.
steps.margin_note: Two lines, one for each substance. Keep them separate.

steps.label: Diseases caused
lines: Long use of tobacco causes bronchitis and
It also causes coronary heart disease and
steps.why: The diseases fall into two sets, the breathing set and the heart and stomach set, and grouping them that way makes all four easy to recall in order.
common_mistakes: Writing 'lung problems' instead of naming bronchitis and emphysema.
Leaving out the gastric ulcer, which is not a breathing disease and is often forgotten.
steps.memory_tip: Two in the chest, two below it: bronchitis and emphysema, then heart disease and gastric ulcer.
steps.margin_note: Four named diseases in two short lines. Names carry the mark, not descriptions.

steps.label: Cancers

lines.text: Cancer of throat, lungs and urinary bladder

lines: Tobacco increases the chance of cancer of the
throat, of the lungs and of the urinary bladder.
The urinary bladder is affected because the
harmful substances of tobacco leave the body in
steps.why: Three cancers are asked and the third one surprises students, so the reason it happens — the waste leaves through the urine — is worth one line.
common_mistakes: Naming only lung cancer. Three sites are expected.
Writing that tobacco causes cancer of the liver. The syllabus names throat, lungs and urinary bladder.
steps.memory_tip: Where the smoke goes and where the waste goes: throat and lungs, then urinary bladder.
steps.margin_note: Three named sites in a box, then one line on the bladder. This is the closing mark.

insider_note: This is a list question and the marks follow the list, so write named items in short lines and never a single long paragraph.
